newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikkei likely to hit 22,000 within year-Goldman.
newsitem.headline: Nikkei likely to hit 22,000 within year-Goldman.

text.p: Japan's key Nikkei stock average is likely to reach the 22,000 level within a year's time, Kathy Matsui, chief strategist of the Japan investment research department at Goldman Sachs (Japan) Ltd, told a seminar on Tuesday.

She said expectations for a recovery in corporate earnings and deregulation measures, including moves to reactivate the sluggish real estate market, would help boost the Nikkei average of 225 leading shares.
However, she added that there would be downside risks depending on the speed of deregulation, worries about Japan's financial system and possible weaker consumer spending.

She also said position-adjustment selling of blue-chip shares and selling of futures contracts by investment trust funds, as well as overseas stock movements, might put pressure on the Nikkei stock index.
"We expect the Nikkei to be at the 22,000 level in about 12 months from now," she said.
She said U.S. mutual funds are likely to buy Japanese stocks which have lagged behind the market.
But foreign investors, except for U.S. mutual funds and some European funds, are not going to be aggressive buyers of Japanese stocks in the 1997/98 business year starting in April, she said.
